body: It was this commit (https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/commit/903f5618fecbf0741cd4f5d9eb2c9a21b5b80223) which started to enforce the type casting; the code then moved to another location but it started here
This commit (https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/commit/d0175672733f7ec3dddbc00833b8b2eb032748fd) brought the enforced type cast to its current position
So the solution is to add `'binary' => 'resource'` to types list?
It worked perfectly for me. Since then it will not be cast to string anymore. Which is the default for all unrecognized types!
How do you work with it then?
This problem (https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/issues/2287)  seems to be related to my issue; maybe it should be consolidated to one solution

issue.body:
Table:

```
CREATE TABLE `post` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8;
```

If i do 

```
var_dump(Post::find()->one()->toArray());
```

Result: `id` is `int`

If i do 

```
var_dump(Post::find()->asArray()->one());
```

Result: `id` is `string`

Same for non-primaryKey `int` fields

issue.title: Save object in user session with DbSession and PostgreSQL fails

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
I'm using DbSession with PostgreSQL for session storage in Yii 2.0.1-dev. When I attempted to store an object in the session, I get the error "Exception (Database Exception) 'yii\db\Exception' with message 'SQLSTATE[22P02]: Invalid text representation: 7 ERROR:  invalid input syntax for type bytea",
## Test Case

**Table in PostgreSQL:**

``` sql
CREATE TABLE public.session_frontend ( 
    id                   varchar(40)  NOT NULL,
    expire               integer  ,
    data                 bytea  ,
    CONSTRAINT pk_session_frontend UNIQUE ( id ) 
 );

CREATE INDEX idx_session_frontend_expire ON public.session_frontend ( expire );
```

**In common/config/main.php:**

``` php
    'components' => [
            ...
        'session' => [
            'class' => 'yii\web\DbSession',
        ],
            ...
    ],
```

**In frontend/config/main.php:**

``` php
    'components' => [
        ...
        'session' => [
            'sessionTable' => 'session_frontend',
        ],
        ...
    ],
```

**Create a test class**

``` php
class TestObject extends \yii\base\Object
{
    public $name;
}
```

**Create object and attempt to save it to the session**

``` php
        $test = new TestObject();
        $test->name = 'This is the name of the object';
        Yii::$app->session->set('test', $test);
```

**Result:**
The object is not saved to the session. `print_r($_SESSION)` results in:

``` pre
Array
(
    [__flash] => Array
        (
        )

    [test] => common\models\TestObject Object
        (
            [name] => This is the name of the object
        )

)
1Exception (Database Exception) 'yii\db\Exception' with message 'SQLSTATE[22P02]: Invalid text representation: 7 ERROR:  invalid input syntax for type bytea
The SQL being executed was: UPDATE "session_backend" SET "data"='__flash|a:0:{}test|O:24:"common\models\TestObject":1:{s:4:"name";s:30:"This is the name of the object";}', "expire"=1416641743 WHERE "id"='hdj5648ufpk6d7mjtrh37l5io1'' 
```
## Possible Solution

I was able to resolve this by changing`'data' => $data` to `'data' => base64_encode($data)` in yii\web\SessionDb::writeSession and `return $data === false ? '' : $data;` to `return $data === false ? '' : base64_decode($data);` in yii\web\SessionDb::readSession. I hesitated to submit a pull request with the change because I don't know how it would affect other database engines.

Also I don't know why it's necessary to convert it to plain text in order for Yii to insert it into a bytea field. #2853 may be related.
